claims.assertion: The enacted Act of 26 April 2024 (Dz.U. 2024 poz. 731) implements Directive (EU) 2019/882; core obligations took effect 28 June 2025.
claims.review_note: Existing legislation link retained; official statute reachable in web reader, scope subject to local provisions and transition rules. Accessed 2026-09-24; reachable.

claims.assertion: A dedicated public page comparable to a WAD accessibility statement is explicitly demanded by a Polish competent EAA body.
claims.review_note: Current Unknown preserved. Do not confuse public-sector WAD declarations on agency sites with EAA provider obligations. No explicit demand for a separate public page found in bounded official-source review; verify regulator guidance on this exact question. User's 24 September 2026 follow-up email asked PFRON expressly whether a public company-site accessibility statement is required; the supplied thread contains no reply to that question. Unknown remains.

claims.assertion: Service providers must publicly provide accessible written information in service terms or equivalent document about the service, its use and how it meets accessibility requirements.
claims.review_note: Law directly available; separate government e-commerce page timed out in web reader and only its indexed summary was visible. Polish-language reviewer confirmed 'terms or equivalent' and paper/electronic scope 2026-09-24.

claims.assertion: Providers may supply written conformity information only when a member of the public requests it.
claims.review_note: No on-request-only model established. PFRON Art. 42 consumer request for state-held information is different from provider publication.

claims.assertion: On request of PFRON or a competent sector regulator, a service provider supplies information needed to demonstrate accessibility conformity by the stated deadline.
claims.review_note: Separate from public disclosure under Art. 32(2)(1); reviewed literal rendering by isolated Polish-language agent 2026-09-24.

claims.assertion: A consumer may request from PFRON or the competent regulator the conformity information it holds.
claims.review_note: This is public access to authority-held information under Art. 42, not an EAA provider accessibility-statement page.

claims.assertion: The Polish Act's sector market-surveillance roster does not identify a separate 112 emergency-call authority in Article 38(3).
claims.review_note: 112 is addressed in Art. 80 by amendment to emergency system law; no competent EAA regulator in Art. 38(3) established. Polish wording reviewed 2026-09-24.

claims.assertion: Customs authorities oversee accessibility of products that are to be placed on the market, as part of the market-surveillance system.
claims.review_note: Statutory class, not one named Article 38(3) sector regulator. Listed separately under Products for checks on products to be placed on the market; individual customs offices not exhaustively audited.

claims.assertion: The public can report inaccessibility of covered products/services to PFRON by email; PFRON considers or refers the notice to the competent market-surveillance authority.
claims.review_note: Current PFRON page is reachable; name of receiving authority, sector and purpose explicit. Anonymous reports are allowed per source, but email sender may still be visible and no anonymity assurance is published in table. Polish reviewer corrected 'always forwards' to 'considers or refers'. No form submitted. Original 'Prezes Zarządu PFRON rozpatrzy zawiadomienie lub przekaże zawiadomienie do właściwego organu nadzoru' literally considers the notice or forwards it to the competent authority; final corrected table wording supported by isolated reviewer. PFRON market-surveillance expert Wojciech Bożek's official email dated 4 September 2026 (user-supplied thread 'PD_ Questions about reporting for the EAA.eml') confirms Article 67 notices may be made by anyone including economic operators and non-Polish entities; email dostepnosc@pfron.org.pl and Mój PFRON are Article 67 channels. Mój PFRON is not a mandatory company non-compliance reporting system. Treat private correspondence as attached evidence, not a publicly linked official webpage.

claims.assertion: An economic operator reporting inaccessible retail-banking services may complete the Financial Ombudsman form, sign the generated PDF and email it to dostepnosc@rf.gov.pl.
claims.review_note: Official page reachable; no submission, accepted language other than Polish not verified. Isolated language reviewer narrowed to retail banking, identified signed PDF and email as one available delivery route. Final table says 'Company reports (inaccessible retail banking services)' per isolated 2026-09-24 Polish-language recheck; broader 'Company non-compliance' would overstate the Polish form. Source 'zgłoszenie przez podmiot gospodarczy niedostępności usług bankowości detalicznej' literally means economic operator report of retail-banking inaccessibility. Final exact table wording rechecked by the no-history Polish-language agent: Supported ('Company reports' avoids claiming every form of statutory non-compliance); 'economic operator' would be more literal than 'company' but shared table vocabulary uses Company.

claims.assertion: Company non-compliance routes for UKE, Minister of Digital Affairs, road/rail/air/sea/inland transport authorities have been established.
claims.review_note: The legal obligation is verified; a usable, purpose-specific destination for each named authority was not established within bounded research. Do not repurpose generic contact forms as confirmed statutory filing routes. PFRON's official 4 September 2026 reply says manufacturer/importer/distributor/service-provider non-compliance and corrective-action notices go directly to the respective competent regulator under its own communication arrangements; this supports the distinction but provides no one universal purpose-specific destination. Article 67 PFRON notifications can also be submitted by companies, yet do not replace regulator notifications.

claims.assertion: A purpose-specific company exemption-notification route is published for Poland.

claims.assertion: Under Article 67, PFRON accepts accessibility non-compliance notifications from anyone, including companies and entities established outside Poland; email to dostepnosc@pfron.org.pl is an accepted channel, and Mój PFRON is optional rather than a mandatory company non-compliance reporting system.
claims.review_note: Official PFRON market-surveillance expert Wojciech Bożek, reply dated 4 September 2026 in the user-supplied 'PD_ Questions about reporting for the EAA.eml' thread; inspected 24 September 2026. This is primary correspondence, not a public government page. Also lists post, electronic delivery, telephone, in-person oral/written and Polish Sign Language options. No form submitted.

claims.assertion: Polish is the appropriate language for Article 67 notifications and official communication with PFRON; the official reply does not establish a right to file in English.
claims.review_note: PFRON market-surveillance expert Wojciech Bożek's reply dated 4 September 2026 in user-supplied thread 'PD_ Questions about reporting for the EAA.eml', inspected 24 September 2026; cites the Polish Language Act, Article 5(1)-(2). This is a statement of appropriate official language, not an assertion that PFRON has never processed an English submission. No implication about Financial Ombudsman's language policy.
